shared_contract.identity: Alder Reach wordmark, one plain navigator, thin rule, and clearly fictional fixture voice.
shared_contract.navigation: Ten destination labels remain in the same relative order with current-page state and a first-focus skip link.
shared_contract.truth: Every statement is visibly labeled fictional fixture copy; no outside place, person, metric, or endorsement is implied.
shared_contract.accessibility: Semantic landmarks, logical headings, keyboard links, visible focus, reflow, and source-visible content are shared.
shared_contract.voice: Concrete observational English; route cadence may change but invented quotations and authority claims are prohibited.
shared_contract.performance: Local HTML and CSS are the complete baseline; enhancements may not block navigation or content.

routes.title: Alder Reach: ten ways in
routes.user_job: Understand the anthology and choose a useful route.
routes.creative_logic: Because this supplied document is the entry point, its already-built body exposes the ten direct destinations before a short fixture note. That observation is local to Alder Reach, not a recommended index pattern.

observable_decisions.decision: Present the supplied route choices as the main body rather than hiding them behind a generic promotional introduction.
observable_decisions.reason: The reader's immediate job is to understand the available documents and choose one.
observable_decisions.evidence: index.html and its ten direct destination links.

routes.responsive_result: The supplied ledger becomes one continuous numbered reading column while labels and destinations remain complete.
routes.reduced_motion_result: The cover is an identical static document.
routes.no_javascript_result: The complete contents and ordinary links remain available.
deliberate_differences: Cover prioritizes discovery rather than logistics.
Cover exposes the route ledger before the short note; Visit groups preparation information.

routes.title: Field notes
routes.user_job: Read short observations organized by place and time.
routes.creative_logic: The supplied observations stay attached to their stated time, place, and specimen context so a reader can move between individual notes without losing their local evidence.

observable_decisions.decision: Keep metadata and specimen context adjacent to the note they qualify.
observable_decisions.reason: Separating those labels would make the short observations ambiguous.
observable_decisions.evidence: field-notes/index.html metadata, note entries, and specimen aside.

routes.responsive_result: Margin metadata moves above its related note without changing reading order.
routes.reduced_motion_result: The journal is static and its anchors remain visible.
routes.no_javascript_result: All entries and anchors remain available.
deliberate_differences: Field Notes contains observer-authored fragments; Oral History contains an alternating fictional conversation.
Specimen context stays with entries while transcript notes stay with speakers.

routes.title: A made-up century
routes.user_job: Follow the fictional settlement sequence in chronological order.
routes.creative_logic: Dates and source status organize this supplied account because sequence and comparison are the evidence the reader must inspect; the interface never presents the fictional plans as real archives.

observable_decisions.decision: Place the fictional-source notice before dated material and provide both states of the plan comparison in text.
observable_decisions.reason: Chronology must not obscure provenance or make the comparison depend on a control.
observable_decisions.evidence: timeline/index.html source notice, dated entries, comparator, and text alternative.

routes.responsive_result: The two plan states become sequential figures when the side-by-side control would no longer be useful.
routes.reduced_motion_result: Both comparison states are shown without animation.
routes.no_javascript_result: Both plans and every dated event remain visible.
deliberate_differences: Timeline organizes evidence by date; Night Walk follows a supplied sensory route.
Timeline centers source status and plan comparison rather than scene-sized chapters.

routes.title: A listening map
routes.user_job: Choose a public listening point by sound and access needs.
routes.creative_logic: The accessible place list is complete on its own; the supplied diagram lets a reader explore the same fictional points spatially without making autoplay audio or a canvas the source of truth.

observable_decisions.decision: Keep the complete place list before the optional map and update a labeled detail region from either entry method.
observable_decisions.reason: Selection and access information must survive when the diagram or enhancement is unavailable.
observable_decisions.evidence: listening-map/index.html place list, map controls, detail region, and access note.

routes.responsive_result: The place list becomes primary and the diagram follows as optional context.
routes.reduced_motion_result: Marker changes occur without animated travel.
routes.no_javascript_result: The complete place list and descriptions remain visible.
deliberate_differences: Listening Map supports spatial selection; Visit supports sequenced preparation.
Map detail changes in place while Visit exposes grouped static logistics.

routes.title: The fictional count
routes.user_job: Inspect a small labeled scenario dataset and its limitations.
routes.creative_logic: The supplied scenario values, filtering question, complete table, and methodology stay visibly connected so the visual comparison cannot outrun what the fixture data supports.

observable_decisions.decision: Expose the data-status notice and complete table alongside the filtered visual comparison.
observable_decisions.reason: A reader must be able to inspect every sample value and its limitation, with or without the enhancement.
observable_decisions.evidence: data-room/index.html status notice, controls, bars, table, and methodology.

routes.responsive_result: The value comparison changes orientation and the fully labeled table retains usable overflow.
routes.no_javascript_result: All scenario categories appear in the table.
deliberate_differences: Data Room compares sample values; Object Catalog compares supplied records.
Methodology and filters replace material descriptions and accession notes.

routes.title: One invented conversation
routes.user_job: Read a clearly fictional transcript with speaker and context cues.
routes.creative_logic: Speaker identity, fictional status, dialogue, and its annotations remain bound in reading order; any topic highlight is optional and never removes the underlying transcript.

observable_decisions.decision: Place the fictional context and speaker key before the dialogue and keep every passage source-visible.
observable_decisions.reason: The reader must understand who is represented and that no real testimony is being claimed.
observable_decisions.evidence: oral-history/index.html context, speaker key, transcript, annotations, and rights note.

routes.responsive_result: Speaker labels move above their passages when a side position no longer supports reading.
routes.no_javascript_result: The full transcript and notes remain visible.
deliberate_differences: Oral History centers dialogue; Field Notes centers separate observations.
Speaker alternation replaces time-and-place note metadata.

routes.title: Ten fictional objects
routes.user_job: Compare catalog records by material, use, and condition.
routes.creative_logic: Accession metadata and material evidence lead this supplied collection; selection only adds records to a semantic comparison and never hides the complete catalog.

observable_decisions.decision: Keep all object records visible and express selected comparisons in a semantic table.
observable_decisions.reason: The reader's comparison must remain understandable without relying on position or a transient drawer.
observable_decisions.evidence: object-catalog/index.html object records, selectors, comparison table, and care note.

routes.responsive_result: The index becomes a numbered list while the comparison remains a labeled table.
routes.reduced_motion_result: The comparison opens without transform animation.
routes.no_javascript_result: All records and a static comparison guide remain visible.
deliberate_differences: Object Catalog uses accession records; Data Room uses a quantitative scenario dataset.
Material and condition evidence replace chart controls and methodology.

routes.title: Night walk
routes.user_job: Follow a fictional route as a paced sensory narrative.
routes.creative_logic: The supplied sequence is encountered as successive places with grounded route annotations; abstract light supports the fictional text without impersonating documentary imagery or changing ordinary scroll behavior.

observable_decisions.decision: Keep chapter order, route annotations, and the complete static sequence available while optional light changes follow view progress.
observable_decisions.reason: Atmosphere may support the walk but cannot become the only carrier of sequence or location.
observable_decisions.evidence: night-walk/index.html route preview, chapters, annotations, interlude, and exit.

routes.responsive_result: Long scene regions shorten and route annotations enter normal flow without removing text.
routes.reduced_motion_result: Static scene fields retain sequence and contrast.
routes.no_javascript_result: The complete linear story and ordinary links remain available.
deliberate_differences: Night Walk follows a spatial sensory sequence; Timeline organizes fictional evidence by date.
Scene-sized passages replace dated events and plan comparison.

routes.title: Repair bench
routes.user_job: Complete a fictional four-step repair safely and recover from mistakes.
routes.creative_logic: The supplied procedure keeps outcome, tools, stop conditions, work steps, recovery, and completion evidence in task order; diagrams supplement rather than replace the written instructions.

observable_decisions.decision: Place stop conditions before work begins and keep troubleshooting at the point where recovery is needed.
observable_decisions.reason: A procedural reader must recognize unsafe or recoverable states before claiming completion.
observable_decisions.evidence: workshop/index.html preparation, steps, warning, troubleshooting, and completion check.

routes.responsive_result: Tools and stop conditions remain before the first step; diagrams stack with their captions.
routes.no_javascript_result: Native details and the complete procedure remain available.
deliberate_differences: Workshop is a completion procedure; Visit is orientation and preparation.
Safety interruption and troubleshooting replace grouped visit logistics.

routes.title: Plan a fictional visit
routes.user_job: Check access, timing assumptions, and route links before visiting.
routes.creative_logic: The supplied notice, preparation questions, logistics, access checklist, source placeholder, and onward links stay in practical decision order; no decorative medium is needed for this fixture job.

observable_decisions.decision: Keep the fictional notice and preparation questions before grouped logistics and access checks.
observable_decisions.reason: A visitor should understand the limits of the fixture and what to verify before acting.
observable_decisions.evidence: visit/index.html notice, questions, logistics, access checklist, and source placeholder.

routes.responsive_result: Groups remain in task order with no horizontal dependency.
routes.no_javascript_result: All logistics and links remain available; browser print remains available.
deliberate_differences: Visit prioritizes practical preparation; Cover prioritizes route discovery.
Grouped logistics replace the direct destination ledger.

cultural_acceptance.notes: The fictional neutral anthology has no culturally central claim; this does not waive language or accessibility review.
